summary:
AstroCare is an astronaut health-monitoring platform designed to support crew wellbeing during space missions. Spaceflight exposes astronauts to challenges such as microgravity, radiation, sleep disruption, and physiological changes that make continuous health awareness essential.

AstroCare brings health information into one platform through a Personal Health Twin, daily self-assessments, vital and biomarker monitoring, radiation tracking, emergency assistance, and mission health analytics. It compares health observations against individual baselines to highlight deviations and provides explainable insights to support medical review.

The platform offers dedicated experiences for astronauts, medical officers, and mission commanders, ensuring that each role can access relevant information. Its offline-first approach is designed to support data collection and synchronization during communication interruptions.

By combining health analytics, role-based access, and mission-oriented decision support, AstroCare aims to help teams make more informed decisions and support safer, healthier human space exploration.
details:
AstroCare is a unified space-health monitoring and decision-support platform designed around the health needs of astronauts during space missions.

The platform provides three role-specific interfaces for astronauts, medical officers, and mission commanders. Astronauts can review their health overview, complete daily self-assessments, explore their Personal Health Twin, and monitor configured health indicators. Medical officers can review authorized crew health information, assessments, biomarker trends, alerts, and reports. Mission commanders receive mission-level crew readiness and environmental information.

AstroCare's Personal Health Twin compares current observations with an individual's established baseline using statistical deviation analysis. Its deterministic alert engine identifies configured deviations, while an AI-assisted explanation layer helps users understand the available information without replacing medical judgment.

Additional modules include biomarker tracking, radiation monitoring, emergency assistance, a multi-stressor simulation environment, research exploration, and mission health reporting. An offline-first workflow supports local data capture and queued synchronization during communication interruptions.

The platform is designed with deep-space mission constraints in mind, including communication delays, data availability, role-based access, and the importance of protecting sensitive health information.

AstroCare combines web technologies, interactive data visualization, health analytics, and AI-assisted explanations to make complex astronaut health information easier to understand and review. Its intended impact is to support informed medical oversight and healthier long-duration human spaceflight.
